Appendix J - Street Cross Sections (PDF)
records.text:
Approved Street Name Suffixes
Name
Standard Abbreviation
Description and Stipulations
Alley
ALY
Alleys are public servitudes which generally run behind lots and provide service to homes and businesses, or are otherwise short streets narrower than the standard width. This suffix is generally not used for new streets except in exceptional circumstances.
Avenue
AVE
A road or thoroughfare that serves through traffic, or ingress/egress traffic within a subdivision or subdivisions. This suffix may only be used for east-west oriented streets.
Boulevard
BLVD
A through street; can also be an entrance roadway for a larger subdivision. These roads contain a landscaped central reservation and a minimum of four through traffic lanes. Roadways of this description are required to use this suffix per the Unified Development Code.
Circle
CIR
A side street which has both termini on the same road, creating a loop or crescent.
Court
CT
Short dead end street which terminates in a cul-de-sac. Recommended length is 600 feet or less.
Drive
DR
A road or thoroughfare that serves through traffic, or ingress/egress traffic within a subdivision or subdivisions. This suffix may only be used for north-south oriented streets.
Highway
HWY
Reserved suffix for State-maintained roads only.
Lane
LN
Minor street within a subdivision which may or may not be a dead-end.
Loop
LOOP
A side street which has both termini on the same road, creating a loop or crescent.
Place
PL
Short dead end street which terminates in a cul-de-sac.
Parkway
PKWY
A thoroughfare designated as a major street. These roadways should include a median or central reservation.
Road
RD
A thoroughfare serving primarily rural areas, with a length greater than one-half mile in length.
Street
ST
A road or thoroughfare that serves through traffic or continues across several subdivisions.
Thruway
THWY
A major street with a minimum of four through traffic lanes and a dedicated central reservation.
Walk
WALK
A side street within an older neighborhood. This suffix is generally not used for new streets except in exceptional circumstances.
Way
WAY
Minor street within a subdivision which may or may not be a dead-end.
Appendix J – Street Cross Sections and Approved Street Name Suffixes June 2021
J-2
